app.title: Jidō Kundoku
app.tagline: Classical Chinese, read as Japanese. Paste a passage and get it marked up for reading aloud, with a plain Japanese version alongside.

help.title: Editing the analysis
help.intro: Each character is marked with its part of speech and with the character it attaches to. That analysis is what produces the reading order, the kaeriten and the kakikudashibun, so correcting it corrects all three at once. The examples below are the real thing, not pictures of it: they follow your theme and language exactly as the text does.
help.step.select.title: Select a character
help.step.select.body: Click a character. Its part of speech appears beneath it, and an arrow is drawn from the character it attaches to, labelled with the relation between them. Click it again, or press Escape, to deselect; the arrow keys step to the next character or line.
help.step.pos.title: Change the part of speech
help.step.pos.body: Right-click the part of speech to choose another; the current one is marked. The reading follows from it, so both panels are redrawn at once — 中 as a verb is read ataru, as a noun naka.
help.step.relation.title: Change the relation
help.step.relation.body: Right-click the label on the arrow to choose a different relation. This is what settles whether a character is read before the one it attaches to, and so whether it takes a kaeriten at all.
help.step.head.title: Attach it elsewhere
help.step.head.body: Drag a character onto the one it should attach to. A dashed line follows the pointer, and the character under it lights up as a candidate. On release the relation is renamed by the parser itself, which scores the new attachment just as it scored the original reading.
help.step.root.title: Make a character the main predicate
help.step.root.body: Choose 文の主辞 from the relation menu. A sentence has one main predicate, so everything attached to the old one moves across to the new one and is renamed to suit.
help.step.reading.title: Choose another reading
help.step.reading.body: Right-click the furigana for the character's other readings — on'yomi first, and only those its part of speech admits. They are given in historical kana, as in the text itself.
help.step.undo.title: Undo anything
help.step.undo.body: Every edit can be undone, a change that moved several characters included — those come back in one press. Hold Shift to redo. Edits stay with the text when you save it, and are written into the CoNLL-U file when you download it.
